purpose: Ranked acquisition order for official rest-area, welcome-center, service-plaza and weigh-station datasets. Gate lines 5 and 6.
ranking_basis: Computed from priority-corridor membership weighted inversely by the parking the directory already publishes on each corridor. I-95 dominates because it publishes 4 mappable parking rows nationwide.
network_status: Every agency host, ArcGIS endpoint, FHWA and USDOT host is BLOCKED at this environment egress proxy. No URL here was fetched or verified. Confirm each entry point on arrival.

rules.weigh_station_is_not_parking: A weigh, inspection, scale, check station or port of entry is never counted as truck parking unless the authoritative source explicitly confirms legal parking is permitted.
rules.no_inferred_coordinates: No coordinate from a road midpoint, ZIP centroid, interpolation or geocoder guess.
rules.no_invented_attributes: Space count, hours, restrictions and amenities stay null unless the source states them.
rules.directional_pairs_stay_separate: A northbound and a southbound facility are two facilities and need two coordinates.
rules.toll_authorities_are_separate_custodians: A state DOT rest-area dataset does not contain turnpike or thruway service plazas. Those must be requested from the authority that operates them.

federal.source: FHWA / BTS national truck parking layer (Jason’s Law survey)
federal.agency: Federal Highway Administration / Bureau of Transportation Statistics
federal.why_first: One request covers all 50 states at once. Lower resolution and possibly stale, but it is the only single artifact that can move gate line 5 nationally in one step.
federal.conflict_rule: State DOT data WINS over FHWA on any conflict — the state is closer to the asset. Record the federal layer vintage and never let it override a fresher state dataset.
federal.access_status: BLOCKED at this environment egress proxy
